ruling.reasoning:
Screen first: the chat is two civil messages about traffic (F7, F8, F9) and the complaint only disputes routing; I read the driver's post-trip statement too (F10) and it is equally civil, so safety_concern = none and no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is engaged [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

F3 is the single off-route segment (10:04–10:11, 3.98 km driven against 1.77 km optimal, +2.21 km, up to 1039 m off route), so RD-1's shortest-and-most-direct duty is prima facie engaged [F3][RD-1].

Traffic does not excuse it. RD-4(a) needs a DataMall incident on the replaced stretch reported before the detour; F14 records none, and F15 is fair weather, so the (a) branch fails outright [F14][F15][RD-4]. F11 (Tampines Expressway band 2, 10–19 km/h, 09:48–10:04) runs only up to the moment the diversion begins and, per RD-4(b), a band fact is corroboration only and is not a standalone exemption, so the segment is not excused on this ground [F11][F3][RD-4].

On consent, the rider did send a message before the segment: F7 (10:01) asks specifically "can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?" and F8 (10:01) replies "Sure, no problem." — a rider's own pre-segment message, so RD-5 timing is satisfied [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. But the agreement is of the SPECIFIC named-road kind, not a general "whichever way is faster" licence: it covers driving on Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road. Nothing does — F3 carries no road name, no stop or location message on that road is recorded, and the driver's statement (F10) is a claim of agreement, not consent evidence (G11); the driver's own statement also names a road/place rather than placing the car on a tracked path [F3][F10][RD-5]. Where the record cannot tie an agreed named road to the driven path, the scope of consent is undetermined (RD-5 / G13), so F3 is left undetermined rather than exempt [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not help the driver: this was a driver-proposed route change, and no rider-requested stop was measured in the segment (F7, F8) [F7][F8][RD-3].

That undetermined finding does not change the outcome here. This is a fixed-quote RydeX trip: the billed distance is 9.84 km against an optimal 9.8 km with no surge and no waiting charge, so the extra mileage never entered the fare (F4, F5, F6) [F4][F5][F6][RD-2]. RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only ERP/toll and unpublished post-trip add-ons, and F6's total of $23.18 contains only published items (base $3.90 + distance $13.88 + time $3.93 + platform $1.47), no toll line [F6][RD-2][FARE-1][FARE-2]. Recoverable amount is therefore $0, which under RD-2 yields no_action while recording the RD-1 breach [F4][F6][RD-2][RD-1]. Because the undetermined consent scope changes neither the amount nor the flag, the case need not go to a person on that ground.

The account flag is not engaged: F17 shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days across 960 trips, so RD-6's "repeated" precondition (≥ 1 prior upheld within 90 days) is unmet [F17][RD-6].
